name: Vark: the pressure transept (draft)
brief: A forbidden process chamber reached through a narrow maintenance approach. A crescent of pressure architecture frames an ominous hatch; the cluttered service bay sits to one side rather than repeating props symmetrically.

art_direction.mood: Oppressive industrial ritual, a laboratory repurposed as a shrine
art_direction.focal_point: The containment crescent and round pressure hatch at the far end of the approach
art_direction.composition: Native-size tunnel frames create an offset narrow approach, a broad chamber, and an asymmetric side bay. Keep the left approach and chamber foreground comparatively empty. Tall service panels and the curved bulkhead supply the silhouette.
alternatives: The breach at the sump: an L-shaped approach and deliberately empty rift recess
The extraction gantry: overhead machinery and a low route, pending supported-stacking investigation
missing_assets: An original extraction-machine hero sculpt, not a primitive stand-in
A suitable victim or operator figure with appropriate rights
A separate original support for the flat console if a freestanding station is desired
fit_notes: Frames are approximately 80 mm modules, not official 50.8 mm E floors; do not rescale.

Trimesh processed/welded topology reports non-watertight meshes for Frame 2x1 A, Frame 2x1 D, and Bulkhead 24 (Doorway Closed). OpenSCAD exact Boolean rendering also reported open-mesh errors. These unchanged source files require slicer review; raw-surface previews do not certify them.
Visual draft only. Frame seams, curved-wall seating, standing areas and connectors need physical verification.
No purchased meshes are fused or modified; no combined production STL is exported.
